rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means one member of a pair in relation to its counterpart; each is individually a zawj, while the two together are zawjān or zawjayni.
rows.anchor: İkisine birden “zevcân, zevceyn” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight individual animals are male and female sheep, goats, camels, and cattle, making four pairs but eight zawj.
rows.anchor: ikisi koyun, ikisi keçi, ikisi deve, ikisi sığır cinsinden olmak üzere erkek ve dişi dört çift

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage models extracting and refining the effective cause: classify the livestock and test sex and pregnancy as possible grounds of prohibition, showing none makes them forbidden by nature.
rows.anchor: bir müctehidin kıyâs-ı fıkhî ile bi’l-ictihâd isbât-ı ahkâm edebilmesinin esası da böyle tahrîc ve tenkīh-i menâttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Analogy alone cannot establish lawful and unlawful rulings: its legal cause must be traced to a fixed basis, and only revelation can establish that basis.
rows.anchor: yalnız bu aklî usûlün, yani kıyâsın kâfi olmayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maytah is an animal that died without ritual slaughter, including those strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, or eaten by a predator.
rows.anchor: kendi kendiye ölene, münhanikaya, mevkūzeye, mütereddiyeye, natîhaya, canavar yiyene hepsine şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spilled blood is prohibited, but liver, spleen, and blood remaining in the vessels after slaughter are outside this category.
rows.anchor: ciğere, dalağa ve zebihten sonra damarlarda kalmış olan bakiyeye şümûlü yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pork is rijs, meaning impure; by the stated rationale, every kind of filthy thing is even more clearly forbidden, as 7:157 also states generally.
rows.anchor: Bu ta‘lîlden anlaşılır ki ne kadar pis şeyler varsa hepsi evleviyetle haramdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rijs rationale also indicates the prohibition of carrion and spilled blood; wine is rijs too, so intoxicants fall under it.
rows.anchor: hamr da ‘rics’ olduğu için bu ta‘lîlde müskirât dahi dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 6:120 shows rijs is broader than outward filth, encompassing inward impurity as well; inner as well as visible corruption is forbidden.
rows.anchor: rics dahi zâhir ve bâtın olmaktan e‘amdır

words: أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase primarily means an animal slaughtered while invoking someone other than God; fisq also encompasses related forbidden practices.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın gayrisinin ismi zikr olunarak kesilenler demektir

words: أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By 6:121, deliberately omitting God's name at slaughter is fisq; 5:3 likewise treats sacrifices at altars and divination by arrows as akin to offerings to other than God.
rows.anchor: amden metrûkü’t-tesmiyenin, kezâlik Sûre-i Mâide âyetindeki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A starving person with no lawful food may eat prohibited food under necessity, provided they do not seize another needy person's food or exceed necessity.
rows.anchor: yiyecek bir helâl bulamaz da mahmasa hâlinde sevk-i zarûretle bunlardan yemek ıztırârında kalırsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In necessity, all forbidden foods may be eaten except where one commits injustice or transgression; for everyone else, those limits are forbidden all the more.
rows.anchor: bâğī ve nütecâviz olmadığı, yani diğer bir muztarrın elindekini almadığı ve yemekte zarûret miktarını tecavüz eylemediği hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking another's property and exceeding the applicable limit through waste are universally forbidden; harming oneself is forbidden even more clearly.
rows.anchor: başkasının malını yemek ve bir de zarûrette zarûrete göre, vüs‘atte vüs‘ate göre haddini tecavüz edip israf eylemek ale’l-ıtlâk ve umûm için haramdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general grounds of prohibition are rijs, fisq, injustice, and transgression; these return to material or spiritual, outward or inward harm under divine judgment.
rows.anchor: illet-i hurmetin rics, fısk, bağy, te‘addî bu dörtten birine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Predatory beasts and birds, vile vermin, and poisons are prohibited as applications of these grounds.
rows.anchor: Yırtıcı canavarların ve kuşların ve haşerât-ı habîsenin ve zehirlerin hurmeti de hep bu illetlerle bu asıllara müteferri‘dir

words: لَآ أَجِدُ فِى مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ مُحَرَّمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the time this verse was revealed in Mecca, the listed items were the only food prohibitions then in force.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin nüzûlüne kadar taâma ait olarak bunlardan başka haram bulunmadığı muhakkaktır

words: لَآ أَجِدُ فِى مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ مُحَرَّمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although later revelation could add detail, many exegetes regard the verse as decisive; later texts clarify and derive its categories rather than abrogate its restriction, also supported by 2:173.
rows.anchor: bundaki hasrı nesheylememiş, belki bunu tavzih ve tefrî‘eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that the exception is disconnected and therefore does not restrict the rule, since 2:173 also uses the emphatic restrictive particle innamā.
rows.anchor: istisnâ munkatı‘dır, bu ise kasr ifade etmez” demesi de muteber olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If matʿūmāt includes drinks, the rijs rationale already points to wine and intoxicants being prohibited in Mecca.
rows.anchor: “mat‘ûmât” tâbirinin meşrûbâta dahi şümûlü kabul edilirse

words: لَآ أَجِدُ فِى مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ مُحَرَّمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report places this verse among a few Medinan verses in the sūra; on that dating, its status as un-abrogated is even clearer.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin Medenî olan birkaç âyet cümlesinden olduğu hakkında da bir rivayet vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the verse is decisive, applying rijs, fisq, injustice, and transgression to less obvious cases still requires exegesis and identifying the effective cause.
rows.anchor: Ancak böyle olması rics, fısk, bağy, te‘addî illetlerinin bazı şeylerde tahakkuku hafî olabileceği cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zufur means nail, but Arabic distinguishes hoof, split hoof, camel pad, and the claws of predators or predatory birds; whether the word literally covers all is disputed.
rows.anchor: tırnak demektir. Fakat Arapça’da muhtelif hayvanların tırnaklarına ayrı ayrı isimler verilmiş olduğu için

rows.speaker: Kāmûs
rows.claim: The lexicon says mihlab is the claw of predatory beasts and hooked claw of predatory birds; one view reserves zufur for non-hunting birds, while the famous view makes it broader than mihlab.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’ta der ki: “Mıhleb yırtıcı canavarların pençesine ve yırtıcı kuşun çengeline denir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sparrows and domestic hens unquestionably have zufur; hawks and falcons unquestionably have mihlab, while their inclusion among zufur is disputed.
rows.anchor: serçe, tavuk bi’l-ittifak zî zufur; atmaca, şahin bi’l-ittifak zî mıhleb ve bi’l-ihtilâf zî zufurda dâhildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling hooves zufur is metaphorical but accepted; Turkish tırnak is similarly broad, though the unqualified phrase tırnaklı hayvan colloquially suggests predators.
rows.anchor: hâfire, zılfa zufur veya zî zufur ıtlâkı mecaz olduğu da tefsirlerde beyan olunuyor

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī takes the immediately suggested sense as clawed predators, including predatory beasts and birds and hunting animals.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî bu âyette de bu mânanın mütebâdir olduğuna kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, İbn Cübeyr, Katâde ve Süddî
rows.claim: These authorities instead identify animals whose toes are not spread out, such as camels, ostriches, ducks, and geese; Zeccâc also prefers this view.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid ve İbn Cübeyr ve Katâde ve Süddî’den ise bunun aksine deve ve deve kuşu ve ördek ve kaz vesâire gibi parmakları açık olmayan hayvanlar diye menkuldür

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase refers specifically to camels.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd bundan maksat bilhassa deve olduğunu

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: Dahhāk identifies ostriches and wild asses.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk devekuşu ve himâr-ı vahşî olduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: Kelbî
rows.claim: Kalbī defines the class by animal kind: clawed birds, hoofed quadrupeds, and fanged predators.
rows.anchor: Kelbî “tuyûrdan her zî mıhleb, devâbdan her zî hâfir

rows.speaker: Kutebî
rows.claim: Kutaybī equates zufur here with hoof and says hoofed quadrupeds are included by metaphor.
rows.anchor: Kutebî “burada zufur, hâfir menzilesindedir

rows.speaker: Sa‘leb
rows.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes non-hunting animals with zufur from hunting animals with mihlab.
rows.anchor: Sa‘leb “sayd etmeyen zî zufur, sayd eden zî mıhlebdir” demiş

rows.speaker: Nakkāş
rows.claim: Naqqāsh objects that Thaʿlab's distinction is not consistent, since lions also have zufur.
rows.anchor: Nakkāş da “bu muttarid değildir, zira arslan zî zufurdur” demiş

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī interprets the term as animals with toes, including camels, birds, and predators; many exegetes prefer this view, which excludes one-hoofed horses.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî de “deve, tuyûr ve sibâ‘gibi parmaklı olanlar” diye tefsir etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although most exegetes include camels and hoofs may also be called zufur metaphorically, Elmalılı reads the phrase broadly as all nail-bearing animals except cattle and sheep.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı bizim anladığımıza göre كُلَّ ذِى ظُفُرٍۢ bakar ve ganem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad reading fits the contrast: Jews held that animals both cud-chewing and split-hoofed were lawful, leaving other kinds forbidden to them.
rows.anchor: Yahudîler geviş getirmekle beraber çatal tırnağı bulunan hayvanların helâl ve bu iki vasıf bulunmayan hayvânâtın haram olduğunu söylemekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That Jewish criterion would also make fish forbidden, although fish were not prohibited to them, showing their own account of the restrictions was inaccurate.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki balık tahrim edilmemiş olduğu cihetle Yahudîlerin kendi ifadeleri kendilerine haram kılınanların târifi husûsunda sâdık değil demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's contrast excludes fish yet signals that the restriction included swine, predators, single-hoofed animals, camels, and all birds, intensifying the Jews' dietary constraint.
rows.anchor: hınzır ve yırtıcı hayvanlarla beraber tek tırnaklıların ve devenin ve bütün kuşların dahi kendilerine haram kılındığını iş‘âr etmektedir

words: وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited cattle and sheep fats are suet or caul fat and kidney fat; fats borne on the back, in the entrails, or mixed with bone remain permitted, including tail fat.
rows.anchor: veya havyalarının, yani bağırsaklarının hâmil olduğu yağlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These foods were originally lawful; God later imposed the restriction as punishment for Jewish transgressions, including killing prophets, usury, obstructing the path, consuming illicit wealth, and reversing lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: bağy ü zulümleri katl-i enbiyâ, ahz-ı ribâ, hak yolundan men‘, ekl-i suht, helâlı haram

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's truthfulness covers reports, promises, and threats, so the report of punitive prohibition is true; those who invert God's rulings ultimately face deprivation.
rows.anchor: İhbârda da sâdıkız, va‘d ü va‘îdde de sâdıkızdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Jews deny that these restrictions were imposed as punishment, the author points to 3:93 concerning Israel's own earlier restrictions.
rows.anchor: hayır, bize tahrim edilenler böyle değil idi” veya “bu tahrim sonradan bağyimizin cezâsı olarak değil ta aslından böyle idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy is vast: He does not punish every sin immediately and accepts repentance, but criminals cannot avert His punishment if they persist.
rows.anchor: Cebr ü tazyîki sevmez, her masiyete hemen muâhaze edivermez, tevbeyi kabul eder

words: وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُۥ عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals may be given time, but persistence eventually turns their latitude and choice into hardship and compulsion, and they cannot escape the punishment.
rows.anchor: nihâyet o rahmet-i vâsi‘adan mahrum ve bir azâba mahkum olurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine commands, prohibitions, lawful status, reward, and punishment concern voluntary acts, not acts done under compulsion; decree therefore does not mean sheer determinism.
rows.anchor: emr ü nehiy, hıll ü hurmet, sevâb ü ikāb ıztırâriyyâta değil, ihtiyâriyyâta ta‘alluk eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordaining chosen acts means ordaining the servant's choice and ordering divine will with it, not imposing pure compulsion.
rows.anchor: Böyle ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyenin takdir ve halkı ihtiyâr-ı abdi takdir ve meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though no act occurs without God's will, a criminal act's concurrence with that will reflects the criminal's approval, not God's pleasure, as 6:113 says.
rows.anchor: cürmün takdir ve meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeye iktirânı Allah’ın rızâsı değil, mücrimin rızâsı nokta-i nazarındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God disapproves of crime and assigned punishment; He also gave people discernment, insight, messengers, scripture, reason, and wisdom to distinguish right from wrong.
rows.anchor: insanlara idrak, basiret, risâlet, kitap, akıl ve hikmet de vermiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's allowing a person to pursue a chosen crime serves that person's will and establishes accountability, rather than showing divine approval; initial respite is mercy but its outcome is punishment.
rows.anchor: abdin rızâsını is‘âf ve meşiyetini infaz ile mes’ûliyetini tahkik içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 6:122, 6:107, 6:112, and 6:137 do not imply that acts God permits or wills are pleasing to Him; using them to excuse sin or deny truth is a false inference.
rows.anchor: buyurulduğundan dolayı “Allah dilemese idi fülân cürüm yapılamazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine pleasure must be sought in God's commands and prohibitions, not inferred from His willing or creating an act; His will includes punishment as well as mercy.
rows.anchor: Rızâullâhın delîlini meşiyyet-i halkında değil, emr ü nehyinde aramalıdır
